note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count and address below comes from one Lehi City page, its parks page, where each park has an "Address:" line and an amenity sentence in which the City counts what it has - "2 pickleball courts", "6 pickleball courts", "1 pickleball court". Four of the six parks also have a page of their own that repeats the sentence, and those were read too. Where the City is silent - on price, lighting, surface, hours and indoor or outdoor at every one of the six, and on parking at four of them - this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking: Lehi's parks page names parking at two of these six parks, and at neither in any detail. Olympic Park's amenity sentence ends "designated parking, walking path that connects to the Jordan River Trail", and Centennial Park's ends "playground, and designated parking." That is the whole of it: a designated lot exists at each, with no capacity, no fee and no hours attached. At Allred Park, Holbrook Farms Park, Stagecoach Large Park and Watercress Park the word does not appear, and this site does not read a lot off an aerial photograph or infer one from the size of the place. The City does use the word elsewhere on the same page - Salix Park and Spring Creek Park, neither of which publishes here, both list "parking" - so the silence at the other four looks like a choice about what to list rather than an accident, though it is recorded as a gap either way. What the page does say about arriving is who has the restrooms. Allred Park lists "restrooms", Holbrook Farms Park lists "Restrooms" and Olympic Park lists "Restroom", singular. Centennial, Stagecoach Large and Watercress list none, and rather than read that as a no, this site records nothing. Holbrook Farms is the one park of the six with a "water fountain" in its sentence. A bike rack, a gate, a closing time - everything else about the trip is unstated at all six.
slots.peak_hours: The City publishes no opening hours and no closing time for any pickleball court in Lehi, and nothing about when the courts are busy. It is not a page that never states hours: on the same list Lehi Sports Park carries "Hours: Open until dusk" and the Pointe Meadow Skate Park is "open to the public from 7:30 a.m. to dusk". None of the six parks with counted pickleball courts carries a line like that, so the absence is the City's and this site leaves it as one. Lighting is the same story with a trap in it. The word appears at two of the six, and both times it belongs to a pavilion: Centennial Park's sentence reads "pavilion lighting" between the electrical outlets and the BBQ grills, and Holbrook Farms Park's reservable Food Truck Alley has "food court string lights, pavilion lighting". Olympic Park's large pavilion has "manual lights". None of those is a statement about a court, and none is published here as one. So no Lehi venue is recorded as lit, none is recorded as unlit, and there is no page of lit courts for the city. What the page does settle is whether you can book. Allred, Holbrook Farms and Olympic sit under "RESERVABLE PAVILIONS", and each entry ends "Reservations are for pavilion use only. All other amenities are open to the public." Centennial, Stagecoach Large and Watercress sit under "NON-RESERVABLE PARKS", where nothing can be booked at all. Either way a court cannot be held in advance, which is what this site calls open play. With six courts Holbrook Farms can run a rotation; the three two-court parks and Centennial's single court are a game, and whoever arrives second waits.
slots.surface_condition: Nothing on the City's parks page says what any of these sixteen courts is made of, and nothing says whether they are indoor or outdoor. The amenity sentences are inventories - a pavilion, its tables, a trash can, a playground, the courts - and an inventory does not describe a slab. This site does not fill the gap from the word "park", so Lehi's indoor and outdoor totals stay empty and there is no outdoor page for the city. What the sentences do settle is what each court is. The City counts pickleball courts and tennis courts as separate things: Watercress Park has "2 pickleball courts, 1 tennis court", written side by side, so its two are not lines on the tennis court. Eagle Summit Park, on the same page, has "a tennis court" and no pickleball at all, and its sentence is asserted on every build so that if the City ever adds pickleball to it the park is read again rather than missed. The counts are digits everywhere they publish, down to Centennial's "1 pickleball court"; Northridge Park's "a pickleball court" is a label rather than a number and is refused for it. Olympic Park's "3 pickleball courts" is an odd number for a block, and the City does not say how the three are laid out. Stagecoach Large is the one park of the six with "1 full basketball court"; Allred and Centennial have half courts.
slots.local_scene: Sixteen verified courts across six City parks, and the City's own page counts more than that. Lehi lists every park it has on one page under two headings, and it opens with the question this page is here to answer - "Where is the nearest playground? What parks have pickleball?" - before sending readers to a Lehi Amenities Map. The list counts courts at eleven parks - twenty-eight in digits at ten of them, plus Northridge Park's "a pickleball court" - and this site can publish six of the eleven. Holbrook Farms Park has six, the largest set the City counts at any park in Lehi; Olympic Park has three; Allred Park, Stagecoach Large Park and Watercress Park have two each; Centennial Park has one. The other four parks with a stated number are refused on their addresses. Shadow Ridge Park's "4 pickleball courts" sit at "3050 W. Traverse Mountain Blvd", Salix Park's "4 pickleball courts" at "3109 W. Allred Dr.", Spring Creek Park's "3 pickleball courts" at "2108 S Bullrush Pkwy" and South Creek Park's "1 pickleball court" at "1987 West 1450 South", and neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap finds any of those four addresses as the City writes them. A count at an address nobody can place does not publish. Northridge Park is refused twice over: "a pickleball court" is an article, not a number, and "2333 W. Northridge Dr" resolves nowhere either. Gateway Park's sentence says "pickleball" with no number at all, a flag rather than a count. So the City's stated inventory is twelve courts larger than the published sixteen, and the gap is in the addresses rather than the courts. Lehi is the second city in Utah to be published here, after St. George, and the first in Utah County; Orem is published alongside it. Nothing here is priced and nothing is called free. "All other amenities are open to the public" is the City's sentence at the reservable-pavilion parks, and open to the public is not a price, so the fee stays unstated at all six and there is no free page for the city.

best_for.heading: Best if you want enough courts for a rotation
best_for.text: Holbrook Farms Park has six pickleball courts, the largest count the City states at any park in Lehi, in its own sentence: "Restrooms, playground with swings, 6 pickleball courts, water fountain, walking path(w/benches), small pavilion (non-reservable w/2 tables)". Six is enough for a rotation. The large pavilion can be reserved; the courts cannot, and are open to the public. Price, lighting, surface and hours are not stated.

best_for.heading: Best if you want stated parking and a trail to walk off the game
best_for.text: Olympic Park has three courts on the west side of Lehi and is one of two published parks where the City names parking: "designated parking, walking path that connects to the Jordan River Trail". A restroom, three soccer fields and a fire pit share the park. The pavilion and the fields can be reserved; the courts cannot. Price, lighting, surface and hours are not stated.

best_for.heading: Best if you want pickleball and tennis in the same park
best_for.text: Watercress Park in south Lehi has two pickleball courts counted beside "1 tennis court" and "8 Horseshoe pits", so the two are pickleball courts in their own right rather than lines on the tennis court. It sits under the City's non-reservable parks, so nothing here can be booked. Two courts is a game, not a rotation. Price, lighting, surface and hours are not stated.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Lehi have?
faqs.a: Sixteen verified across six City parks: six at Holbrook Farms, three at Olympic, two each at Allred, Stagecoach Large and Watercress, and one at Centennial. The City's page counts twelve more at four parks - Shadow Ridge and Salix with four each, Spring Creek with three and South Creek with one - whose addresses neither resolver finds as written, so they are not published.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in Lehi?
faqs.a: Not stated. The City prices nothing on its parks page and calls nothing free. Its sentence at Allred, Holbrook Farms and Olympic is "Reservations are for pavilion use only. All other amenities are open to the public.", and the other three parks sit under "NON-RESERVABLE PARKS". Open to the public is a rule about access, not a price, so the fee is unknown at all six and there is no free page for Lehi.

None is stated to be. The word appears twice among the six parks and both times it belongs to a pavilion - "pavilion lighting" at Centennial Park and at Holbrook Farms Park's Food Truck Alley - and Olympic Park's pavilion has "manual lights". None of those is a court, so lighting is recorded as not verified at every venue, and no venue is recorded as unlit either.

No. At Allred, Holbrook Farms and Olympic the City says "Reservations are for pavilion use only. All other amenities are open to the public." Centennial, Stagecoach Large and Watercress are listed under "NON-RESERVABLE PARKS", so nothing there can be booked. No court in Lehi can be held in advance, and the City publishes no hours for any of them.

faqs.q: Why are Shadow Ridge, Salix, Spring Creek and South Creek not listed?
faqs.a: Because their addresses do not resolve. The City counts four, four, three and one court at them, but "3050 W. Traverse Mountain Blvd", "3109 W. Allred Dr.", "2108 S Bullrush Pkwy" and "1987 West 1450 South" are found by neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap as written. Northridge Park is refused too: "a pickleball court" is a label, not a number, and its address resolves nowhere either. Gateway Park says "pickleball" with no number.
